cells.tense: You are tending something that is coming along, and you can see the work it has taken.
cells.act: take pleasure in the grown thing
cells.ask: Give ten minutes to something you carried or raised. Not to improve it — just to be near what grew.
cells.core:
You test your commitments by staying with them, and the tests have been passing. What you have been tending is coming along without much steering from you now, and you can see how much of the work was yours. Care that has not exhausted you is care that was measured right.
Take pleasure in a grown thing. Sit with something you have carried or raised for ten minutes, without improving it. Enjoyment is the entire point of the ten minutes. What you enjoy, you keep feeding. Tiredness is not the proof that the care was real, and noticing what is flourishing now tells you what to carry next.
cells.sheetLine: The care you gave shows, and you can look at it.
cells.verb: testing what you are committed to by staying in contact with it
cells.place: where care for what is growing is tended

cells.tense: You will be bracing for a test of your commitment that has not arrived yet, and it is arriving faster in your head than anywhere else.
cells.act: show someone the way you found
cells.ask: Show one person the route you found for the thing you are good at — one route, plainly — then let them walk it.
cells.core:
You are standing over what is growing with a plan for how it should be going, and the plan is moving faster than the growing is. More effort goes into steering than the thing asks for. Somewhere under the urgency, curiosity has gone quiet. There is a way you found yourself, and you have not handed it to anyone.
Show someone the way you found it. One route, plainly, once, then let them walk it without your help. Whatever happens on their walk is theirs to read, not a verdict on what you know. Showing the route is how you learn what you actually know, rather than what you are still rehearsing.
cells.sheetLine: You have a route that works and you are keeping it.

cells.tense: You were carrying something for a while, and you have set it down, and your hands are still shaped around it.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Do a small piece of help a person already needs, start to end. Finish it, then stop.
cells.core:
You are past something you were committed to, and the strength that carried it has not landed anywhere. Being told to rest and receive would not get through. What you can still do is lift something else — not to make your old load matter, but because your hands work when they have a weight in them.
Give one concrete piece of help and finish it. A small task a person needs done, start to end, and then stop. It is not a way back to what you set down. It is your strength going somewhere real again, and knowing your own strength is what comes before anything fills the space it left.
cells.sheetLine: The strength is still there, with nothing to land on.

cells.tense: Things are coming up around you because of care you don't count, and you keep calling whatever happens luck or somebody else's doing.
cells.act: let the abundance be seen and used
cells.ask: Set aside a result that came from your care. Count it as yours where someone can hear it, once.
cells.core:
Things near you come along, and the account you give is that it happened without you. The earliest form of your way is already showing: you hold space for something small without clutching it, and it grows, and you call that nothing. Enjoying what careful tending produced is not claiming credit you haven't earned. It is the plainest fact about the ground you keep.
Put what you caused to grow where it can be seen and used. A result that came from your care, named as yours, where someone can hear it. It will feel like bragging. Say it anyway. A thing that is only fed while it goes unnoticed has no owner, and you have been its owner the whole time.
